html:
A stone tower the Genoese built in 1348 at the highest point of their walled colony of Galata, across the Golden Horn from Constantinople. They called it the Tower of Christ.

Galata was a trading town that Genoa held under treaty with the Byzantine emperors. Its merchants ran much of the Black Sea grain and slave trade, and the tower watched over the harbour and the colony's walls.

In 1453 Galata stayed formally neutral during the Ottoman siege, and it surrendered to Mehmed II without a fight. The Ottomans kept the tower, used it as a prison and later as a fire watch post over Istanbul. It has been rebuilt after fires several times, and today it is a museum and one of the city's landmarks.
sum: A stone tower the Genoese built in 1348 at the highest point of their walled colony of Galata, across the Golden Horn from Constantinople. They called it the Tower of Christ.
